summary.name: Screen Printing. Supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Flat spot-color screen-print look using a small set of discrete inks, strong positive-negative shapes, and visible paper. Slight handmade edge variation supports the print treatment. Ink coverage and overprint relationships define the image, and color layers are revealed without making smooth gradients the main feature.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit source pairings: style-103 for loopable posters usable as stills, such as gig posters, festival announcements, and limited-edition promos; style-043 for silhouette-based narrative posters, outdoor and travel themes, and title sequences. Other uses such as product or editorial introductions are inferred, not stated.
summary.limitations: Smooth gradients must not become the main feature, and lettering stays sharp rather than textured. Source states simulated appearance is not evidence of physical print production or validated physics. Body text should use the main background, since the accent pairing misses the 4.5 target. Duration, resolution, frame rate, and aspect ratio are unspecified; examples are optional.
summary.palette: Authored suggestions, not approved exact colors: background #F4E9D4 (natural paper layout role), foreground #233E45 (dark ink layout role), accent_1 #B95A43 (rust, decorative). Keep three discrete inks with no gradients enabled. Foreground/background contrast is 9.452. Accent_1 against background is 3.789, so use it decoratively only. Supplied task or brand colors override these, and assets must not be recolored.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Smooth, coherent movement is encouraged where the action benefits, while deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds are preserved. Ink layers reveal in plausible print order. Video state derives from seekable composition time. Live interaction is unspecified for video; a responsive interactive delivery is inferred to pause loops under reduced motion. Springs and bounce are not added automatically.
summary.audio: Unspecified for this style. Suggest audio from the topic, audience, and explicit requirements, such as music, voiceover, sound effects, or silence. Do not default to instrumental music. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals, and verify balance, absence of clipping, and picture sync. No audio assets are supplied.
summary.assetRequirements: Artwork must be separated into spot-color layers, with a fixed ink-edge texture per plate and controlled overprints. Lettering remains sharp. Fonts and assets must be loaded locally before rendering. Missing task artwork, exact copy, or authorized audio must be stated as missing. Pillow or Sharp may prepare raster crops, masks, and textures. Canvas and SVG are unspecified as the final renderer for any given task.
summary.combinations: Use alone for bold flat-ink graphics. Pair with style-103 for loopable posters that must work as stills, using two inks and paper only, plausible print order, and matched loop endpoints. Avoid gradients, moving headlines, and mismatched loops. Pair with style-043 for silhouette narratives with one fixed edge texture per plate. Avoid 043's slate accent and merged figures.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary composition and export pipeline, with a paused seekable GSAP timeline registered per composition. Remotion is a conditional fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. SVG is the style renderer. Motion is optional for DOM or SVG layers. chroma.js validates colors and contrast. Delivery requires frame, audio, and loop checks.
